== Finding ==
No 02A7 interface declares a 90-byte feature report (report id 0) on macOS. zexrox opens exactly
one collection on "interface 3" and sends report id 0 + 90 bytes there (zexrox
native/host.py:456-464, :446). Which macOS interface is USB interface 3, and whether any
interface is hidden from the HID stack, is not yet known.

IOUSBHostInterface@1 class 3 → AppleUserUSBHostHIDDevice (1/6, MaxFeature 1) → event service RazerGenericHIDDriverKit (com.razer.appengine.driver)   = kbd-multi
IOUSBHostInterface@2 class 3 → AppleUserUSBHostHIDDevice (1/2, MaxFeature 0) → event service RazerGenericHIDDriverKit (com.razer.appengine.driver)   = kbd-mouse
IOUSBHostInterface@3 class 3 → NO child driver at all (registered, matched, active; no HID device, no user client)
IOUSBHostInterface@4 class 3 → AppleUserUSBHostHIDDevice (0x59/1, MaxFeature 51)   = kbd-lamparray
IOUSBHostInterface@5 class 3 → AppleUserUSBHostHIDDevice (0xFF00/0, MaxFeature 0)  = kbd-vendor

== Finding (updated) ==
USB interface 3 — the one zexrox drives on Windows with report id 0 + 90 bytes — has no HID driver
bound on macOS, so no IOHIDDevice exists for it and Chrome's WebHID cannot enumerate it.
[HYPOTHESIS] reasons: the interface lacks the interrupt-IN endpoint macOS's HID driver needs, or its
descriptor is rejected. Interface 3 is HID class (3), which WebUSB treats as a protected class for
claimInterface(); whether device-recipient control transfers reach it is untested.
